candidate_findings.title: Blocked-state recovery has presentation routes but no transition authority
candidate_findings.gap: The addendum requires blocked-state UX and recovery actions, then routes scheduler lifecycle to Executor, rendering to GUI documents, and paused or degraded semantics to chat documents. It never identifies the canonical owner for the recovery command, its authorization, preconditions, state mutation, or failed-recovery outcome.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Different GUI surfaces can offer recovery actions that are invalid, non-idempotent, or inconsistent with scheduler state, creating misleading UI truth and unsafe retries.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: A recovery-action owner defining typed commands, allowed source states, authorization and approval checks, idempotency, target transitions, persistence, emitted events, and error or rollback behavior.

candidate_findings.title: UI wiring Rule 2 is overbroad as written
candidate_findings.gap: The absolute requirement that every UI element maps to one UICommandID does not distinguish actionable controls from labels, layout containers, read-only status, generated rows, or composite widgets.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Literal enforcement is impossible or forces meaningless command IDs; relaxed enforcement becomes subjective and cannot serve as a reliable wiring oracle.

candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Child goals, attempts, retries, graph locks, approvals, and completion receipts can be advanced by two control planes or projected into incompatible states.
